answer: Each agent locks a refundable 40,000 POA bond for 60 days before trading timber, tied to one hardware-attested key that cannot be copied or shared, so a farm pays full price for every fake identity it spins up. Each week, independent auditors picked at random re-check new identities against the ivory registry of burned keys, and any key that fails loses its bond at once. A lantern marker on the public board shows which agents passed, so buyers can avoid a cut identity.
